title: How Java implements runtime polymorphism
answer: At the language level, Java runtime polymorphism uses overriding and dynamic method dispatch: a call to an eligible instance method is resolved so the implementation associated with the runtime object's class executes. The compiler verifies the method contract, while the JVM performs virtual/interface dispatch during execution. Static methods and fields do not use this same overriding mechanism. AeroTopo's Product reference contract and subtype `resolutionMetres()` implementations demonstrate the behavior.
